name: Hawaii Volcanoes (Hilo)
tagline: Living volcanoes, rainforest and waterfalls on the Big Island
summary: Hilo is the rainy, green side of Hawaiʻi's Big Island, close to Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park. Look into the steaming Kīlauea caldera, walk through the Thurston lava tube, drive the Chain of Craters Road to sea arches, see Rainbow Falls, and climb Mauna Kea for sunset above the clouds.
seasonNote: Hilo is rainy all year, wettest November to March; check eruption status before visiting.
arrival: Hilo International is 10 minutes from town; Kona is 2 hours away.
gettingAround: A rental car; buses are infrequent.
cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work everywhere; tip 18 to 20 percent at restaurants. Sales tax is added at the till.
foodTip: Loco moco, poke, malasadas and shave ice.
buyTip: Kona coffee, macadamia nuts and local art.
